name: Drusilla
overview: Drusilla is a female figure mentioned in the New Testament as the wife of Felix. Beyond her marital connection, Scripture does not provide additional personal details such as tribal affiliation or specific notes. Her mention is concise and primarily identifies her relational role.
namesAndTitles: The name Drusilla appears once in the biblical record without a provided meaning or divine origin. It is presented simply as a proper name without additional significance noted in the text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Drusilla beyond her being the wife of Felix. No other familial connections are documented in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Drusilla's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to her marriage to Felix, a Roman official.
